literal: Having suffered and suffered, let the inner water dry up, of the eyes that, having desired, wasted away, and wanted, saw him.
translation: Let the tears within these eyes dry up completely after endless suffering, for they are the very eyes that eagerly desired, melted with love, and sought to look upon him.
modern: விரும்பி, உருகி, அவரே வேண்டுமென்று அவரைப் பார்த்த கண்கள், இப்போது துன்பப்பட்டுத் துன்பப்பட்டுத் தங்களுக்குள் இருக்கும் கண்ணீர் வற்றிப் போகட்டும்.
explanation: The heroine is expressing her frustration with her own eyes, which weep incessantly in the absence of her lover. She points out that it was her eyes that initially desired him, melted with love, and insisted on looking at him. Since they brought this longing upon themselves, she declares that they deserve to suffer and weep until their inner tears dry up completely. The repetition of 'uḻantu' emphasizes the intensity of the suffering, while 'iḻaintu' beautifully captures how the eyes (and the lover) waste away or melt in intense desire.
